newsitem.title: USA: Jury selection begins in coma rape case in U.S..
newsitem.headline: Jury selection begins in coma rape case in U.S..

text.p: Jury selection began on Monday in the trial of a New York state nursing home aide accused of raping a comatose patient who later gave birth to a baby boy.
The woman, now 30, remains in a coma, as she has been since a car accident 11 years ago. Her mother is raising the baby, now almost 11 months old.

Prosecutors say the defendant, John Horace, 53, raped the woman in August 1995 when he was a nursing assistant at the Westfall Health Care Facility in Brighton, New York and she was a patient there. He is charged with rape and sexual abuse.
The case is expected to hinge on DNA evidence, which prosecutors say shows a more-than-99 percent probability that Horace is the baby's father.
Authorities tested Horace's blood as well as saliva from an envelope he licked and compared the evidence with amniotic fluid from the woman's womb and with the baby's blood.
Horace's defence attorney, Yolanda Villa, argued at pre-trial hearings that the child was conceived before Horace began working at the nursing home on Aug. 7, 1995.

Prosecutors plan to call a former co-worker of Horace's who says she walked in after he had given the comatose woman a shower. The co-worker said Horace was leaning over the naked woman with a "look of surprise, a startled look" on his face.
The woman was the victim of a car accident in upstate New York while she was a 19-year-old student at Cornell University in Ithaca.
She reportedly opens her eyes and follows movement but is unresponsive and uncommunicative. Doctors say she will never emerge from her vegetative state.
The baby boy, weighing two pounds 11 ounces (1.28 kg) was born through natural childbirth on March 18, 1996.
The baby's grandmother, who has never spoken publicly about the ordeal, is expected to testify at the trial.
Few details are known about the baby's life, but family attorney John Parrinello said the grandmother frequently took the child to visit his mother.

Horace has served prison time for two other sex crimes. He pleaded guilty last year to impersonating a physician at an unlicensed "sex therapy clinic" and was convicted of fondling a 49-year-old multiple sclerosis patient, also at Westfall.
Jurors are not expected to be told about those cases unless he testifies in his own defence.
Courthouse officials expect the selection of 12 jurors and two alternates to take about a week, and the trial is scheduled to be televised on a local cable station.
The victim will be called "Jane Doe" in court, the baby "Baby Doe" and the grandmother "Grandma Doe."
If convicted, Horace faces a maximum prison sentence of eight-and-a-half to 25 years in prison.
